## Context / Problem
normalize_ci_conclusion.sh is a pure function in shell — trivially portable, currently untestable by the Python suite. Its REAL contract is two-input: f(CONCLUSION, FAILURE_OBSERVED) -> vote in {success, failure, cancelled} (never out-of-domain), consumed by .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml.

## Approach
Port to a small stdlib-only Python entry point with unit tests; the workflow call site swaps to the Python invocation. The workflow currently fetches the script via sparse-checkout of exactly 'scripts/normalize_ci_conclusion.sh' (gerrit-verify.yaml:323) and calls it at :340 — update the sparse-checkout path to the new .py file (cone-mode: false so a single-file pattern works) and keep the entry point dependency-free so the single-file checkout still runs without the package installed. Opportunistic priority (lowest tier).

## Scope
- the script + its workflow call site (sparse-checkout path at gerrit-verify.yaml:323 AND the run invocation at :340) + unit tests

## Testing
Table-driven unit test over the script's actual contract f(CONCLUSION, FAILURE_OBSERVED):
- success -> success; failure -> failure; cancelled -> cancelled (FAILURE_OBSERVED irrelevant for these — assert both values)
- skipped x FAILURE_OBSERVED=false -> success (benign im-open fallback)
- skipped x FAILURE_OBSERVED=true -> failure (fail-closed)
- empty CONCLUSION -> failure; unrecognized value (e.g. 'timed_out') -> failure (fail-closed anomaly rows)
- FAILURE_OBSERVED unset defaults to false
Outputs asserted to always be in {success, failure, cancelled}.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Python entry point reproduces the shell mapping exactly as f(CONCLUSION, FAILURE_OBSERVED), including skipped-fallback rows and fail-closed empty/unknown rows.
- [ ] Table-driven tests cover the full contract above (both FAILURE_OBSERVED values for pass-through rows included).
- [ ] gerrit-verify.yaml sparse-checkout fetches the new .py path (cone-mode: false) and the run step invokes it; entry point is stdlib-only so the single-file checkout works; shell file deleted.
